basics.name: Gabriel Lucchesi
basics.label: Machine Learning Engineer
basics.summary: Software engineering and machine learning student at Florida International University, focused on large-scale systems, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI.

work.name: Google - YouTube
work.summary: Large-scale graph modeling and NLP for understanding channel relatedness at YouTube.
highlights: Modeled end-to-end training and online inference pipelines for large-scale JAX-based Siamese Neural Networks for channel relatedness classification on actor relatedness, accounting for hundreds of millions of YouTube users.

Leading development of Message-Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) on YouTube user graphs to proactively predict channel badness through topological and neighborhood-based features of colluding actor clusters.
Reduced manual human reviews for relatedness by content similarity across YouTube by 58% through LLM-as-raters and parameter-efficient encoder-heavy classifiers trained with supervised fine-tuning.

work.name: Google - YouTube
work.summary: Explored LLM post-training methods and reinforcement learning reward models for large-scale comment and channel-wide spam detection.
highlights: Researched LLM post-training approaches that improved caught live-traffic impressions in an adversarial view rate (AVR) setting.
Designed reinforcement learning-based reward models to enhance reasoning and OOD generalization in adversarial environments using Group-Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Created JAX-based utilities to fine-tune Gemma models with LoRA and Reasoning SFT on classification tasks under low TPU HBM constraints.

work.name: NVIDIA
work.summary: Worked on ML infrastructure and GPU scheduling for OSMO, NVIDIA's cloud-based robotics and ML platform.
highlights: Drove development of user-facing modules in OSMO, NVIDIA's ML infrastructure platform for robotics and GPU scheduling.
Implemented workflow-scheduling APIs in Python for integration with a Bazel and Kubernetes backend.
Assisted GEAR's research on video-game agents by analyzing data for training inverse dynamics models.

work.name: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA)
work.summary: Researched embodied AI and reinforcement learning for language-conditioned robotic agents.
highlights: Integrated early fusion-based models into robots for reinforcement learning policies in egocentric, language-conditioned tasks.
Studied sim-to-sim transfer learning for embodied AI models from Habitat-Sim to Isaac Sim.
Aligned multimodal LLM hidden states with previous high-level policy actions expressed in PDDL.

work.name: Florida International University
work.position: Undergraduate Researcher (Advanced Research and Creativity in Honors)
work.summary: Worked on explainable AI and deep reinforcement learning for autonomous control systems.
highlights: Applied attribution algorithms for explainable AI in agent-based deep RL under Sumit Kumar Jha, Ph.D.
Trained a lunar lander agent in a Box2D environment using Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients for smoother engine control.
Used PyTorch's Captum and integrated gradients to analyze attribution maps for RL policies, visualized via a Hugging Face Space.

work.name: Florida International University
work.position: Teaching Assistant, COP 3337 (Programming II) & MAC 2311 (Calculus I)
work.summary: Supported large undergraduate courses in programming and calculus.
highlights: Assisted over 120 students through lectures, office hours, and grading.
Helped students debug programming assignments and reinforce core CS fundamentals.

work.name: AI Guild at FIU
work.summary: Organized and taught AI and ML workshops for a student community at FIU.
highlights: Hosted workshops on deep learning, CUDA, linear algebra, JAX, and PyTorch for a community of 35+ students.
Led reading groups and discussions on research papers as part of semi-weekly projects.
Developed spotlight projects such as GPT-2 124M from scratch and variational autoencoders.

volunteer.summary: Directed INIT FIU, Florida International University’s largest hackathon for student organizers and participants.
highlights: Created the website for ShellHacks 2024, supporting over 1,400 student hackers.
Built a judging system in Streamlit for Sponsors, automating scoring workflows.
Scaled judging latency down significantly via effective database operations and data visualization on project submissions.

publications.name: From Signals to Semantics: A Survey on Time Series Explainability through a Human-Cognitive Lens
publications.summary: Survey paper on time series explainability methods evaluated through a human-cognitive lens, co-authored with collaborators at multiple institutions.

projects.name: Attention Mechanisms
projects.summary: Research project on state-of-the-art attention mechanisms in JAX and Flax.
highlights: Co-wrote and implemented a survey on state-of-the-art attention mechanisms in JAX and Flax Linen.
Engineered neural attention modules for multiple transformer architectures.
Explored multi-headed self-attention, group query attention, multi-query attention, and KV-caching optimizations for efficient inference.

projects.name: Aura
projects.summary: Generative adversarial network and CLIP-based system for real-time emotion-aware avatars.
highlights: Led a team of students to train a live, lightweight StyleGAN model for conditional video generation.
Built a face detection and emotion recognition pipeline with PyTorch achieving sub-second inference.
Aligned emotion embeddings with synthetic video frames using CLIP and integrated WebRTC for real-time IO.

projects.name: Memora
projects.summary: Memory management assistant for IrisBD for Alzheimer’s patients using RAG and multimodal LLMs.
highlights: Co-developed a memory management system in IrisBD using retrieval-augmented generation.
Used OpenCV and image-to-text processing with Qwen2-VL for recognizing people and objects.
Leveraged LangChain to orchestrate multimodal interactions with a Llama 3.1-based assistant and won best generative AI project at HackN’IT.

projects.name: Mimir
projects.summary: Conversational RAG system for accelerator-based reinforcement learning agents using Weaviate.
highlights: Built a chat system over accelerator-based RAG and WeaviateDB for experiment logging.
Integrated with ServiceNow’s challenge at University of Central Florida’s hackathon, KnightHacks.

projects.name: Project DARWIN
projects.summary: Team project exploring OpenAI Gym, MuJoCo, and deep RL for Atari agents.
highlights: Led a six-person team to build an agent framework over OpenAI Gym, MuJoCo, and Gymnasium.
Trained policy networks with Q-learning, deep Q-learning, and DDPG across Atari environments.
Designed a reusable framework to teach agents to play over 100 Atari games from GUI input.

projects.name: Pots n’ Pans
projects.summary: Computer vision-powered recipe recommendation web app.
highlights: Built a Next.js application that uses computer vision to infer ingredients from fridge images.
Deployed a YOLOv8 CNN model under a serverless GPU architecture in RunPod.
Indexed over 300,000 recipes and used image segmentation to query the database.
Won first place for sustainability at Georgia Tech’s Hack GT hackathon.

projects.name: National Conference for Undergraduate Research Talk
projects.summary: Oral presentation on explainability and introspection in deep reinforcement learning.
highlights: Presented work "Opening the Black Box: Explainability and Introspection in Deep Reinforcement Learning" at NCUR.
